Left 4 Dead is a first-person shooter in which the player takes control of one of four survivors; if human players are not available, the remaining survivors are filled by AI-controlled bots. They play through campaigns fighting off the infected—living humans who have been infected with a rabies-like virus that causes psychosis.[2][3] The overarching goal is not to clear infected, but only to reach the next safe area alive. This is compounded by the presence of an "AI Director", who tracks each player's current situation, and will add or remove items and infected in response; with the goal of maintaining constant tension and creating a new experience with each playthrough. 
Left 4 Dead received praise for its replay value, focus on cooperative play, and cinematic feel, although some criticized its limited level selection and lack of narrative. Considered one of the greatest video games ever made, the game won several publication awards

🧟‍♂️ Overview
Left 4 Dead is a cooperative multiplayer FPS set in a post-apocalyptic world overrun by zombies. Developed by Valve, it emphasizes teamwork, survival, and replayability, using an AI system known as the “Director” to dynamically adjust the game’s pacing, enemy placement, and intensity.

🔫 Gameplay
Co-op Focused: You play as one of four survivors, working together to battle hordes of the infected across a series of campaigns.

AI Director: This innovative system changes item locations, zombie spawns, and difficulty in real-time to keep every playthrough unique.

Special Infected: Aside from standard zombies, players face unique enemies like the Hunter, Smoker, Boomer, Tank, and Witch — each with a distinct threat level and tactics required to defeat them.

Versus Mode: Players can also play as infected, adding variety and competition.

🎮 Controls and Mechanics
Classic FPS controls, smooth and responsive.

Friendly fire is enabled even in casual modes, emphasizing coordination.

Healing, reviving, and item sharing are all central to surviving, reinforcing the team-oriented design.

👥 Multiplayer Experience
Best enjoyed with friends or competent teammates.

While bots fill in for absent players, they lack the intelligence and nuance of humans.

Voice chat and teamwork are practically required on higher difficulties.

🎨 Graphics & Atmosphere
The Source engine delivers clean, moody visuals.

Lighting and sound design contribute heavily to a tense, horror-inspired atmosphere.

Campaigns are varied — from rural farmland to dense cities.

🔁 Replayability
High replay value thanks to the AI Director.

Custom campaigns and mods (on PC) expand the game far beyond its base content.

👎 Cons
Limited weapon variety compared to modern shooters.

No significant single-player narrative — the story is minimal and environmental.

Lacks depth in progression or unlocks (no XP or skill trees).

⭐ Verdict
Rating: 9/10
Left 4 Dead is a benchmark in co-op shooters. Its innovative AI Director and tight team mechanics make it a standout even today. Though it lacks modern polish in progression systems or graphics, the core gameplay remains thrilling and endlessly replayable. Best experienced with friends and a mic.

This game is very entertaining and is able to run well on many systems, however, due to the number of effects, unoptimized configs and lockdown of graphical settings, it is not as customizable nor optimized as older Source games, such as Half-life 2, Counter-Strike: Source or even Team Fortress 2.
At this point, pretty much all Source games support OpenGL rendering, which is much faster than the proprietary renderers such DirectX (or Direct3D), even the decent DX9 and 8, however, this support is only included for Linux (and other operating systems similar to ones using Linux); while I would definetely understand gatekeeping this performance (and security) to make people more attracted to free operating systems, I do not believe this is something done for activism/raising awareness, rather just a decision for convenience, which costs basically 75% of performance for Windows users and, even if the Windows version also used OpenGL, Linux, BSD and other free oprating systems would still vastly outperform Windows.

I see this game to be vastly superior to its sequel (Left 4 Dead 2), containing more cohesive and better visuals, better performance, better characters and better campaigns. The darker visuals are ideal to the slower (when compared to Left 4 Dead 2's) gameplay.
Left 4 Dead lacks some additions later implemented into Left 4 Dead 2, however, not to its detriment. Such as lack of melee weapons, less zombies and less special infected, it makes Left 4 Dead much less of a zombie killing sandbox and much more cohesive with its lore and ambience. The disparity between difficulties is not obvious and might be subjective, but Left 4 Dead is less ridiculous than its sequel in relation to that; they both are definetely unfair, technically, considering you're one man (or four if you count your team) fighting hordes of zombies, but zombies in the first game are less janky, lesser in number, while still being threatening since you have no OP melees.

Ahh. Left 4 Dead. One of the most GOATED games of all time back in the late 2000s. A game that was ahead of it's time with SO MUCH DETAIL, but most of us who were teenagers and kids just played the game with joy. We didn't think to appreciate and take in the amount of dedication and love that went into this game and the sequel that came a year after. I was 9 years old, the only games I really played outside of Steam were DOOM, Quake, a bunch of totally legal and legit emulators on the family computer, and my Playstation 2, had over 100 games with the original cases all stacked up inside an old cardboard box just for the PS2. I loved shooters, zombie games, and zombie films. It was a very fun time. 

One day, I decided to go to the electronics store with my father just to peruse and see what cool things were there. I was of course hyper focused on the video games that were on the shelves. That's when I saw it, in all it's glory. A DVD case with the box cover art depicting a decrepit looking hand in the center, the green background that looked like it was scratched up by said hand, and of course, the magical title that popped out and stood out to me. Left 4 Dead is what I read. I walked up to my dad who was in line for checkout, holding the DVD case and tugging at his shirt to get his attention, he looked down at me holding this game in my hand and raising an eyebrow saying: "You want a new video game? You sure? That looks way too violent for you." That of course made me feel a bit sad and I began to walk back to the shelves to put the game back until I heard the magical words from my dad: "Okay. Put it up on the counter and tell the gentleman that you want to buy this game." My dad paid $45 dollars for the game and I walked out a very happy child. From there, the rest was history. 

Only 343 hours into this game, it was the first game I ever bought on Steam and the one way I discovered Steam. While 343 hours may not be a lot to others, it shows how much I love this game and find myself from time to time going back. 17 years that this game has been out and it's still a blast to play Solo and Co-Op. The current gaming industry couldn't even replicate or capture the same lightning in the bottle that was Left 4 Dead and clearly, it has shown. Turtle Rock Studios and their marketing for Back 4 Blood as being the so called "acclaimed creators of Left 4 Dead" was a disaster. I was happy to never have bought Back 4 Blood at a price tag that is still original MSRP, it's not even polished or finished. Claiming to be the "self proclaimed creators of Left 4 Dead" while only being the 2-3% of the original team that MADE Left 4 Dead and handing out an unpolished unfinished turd that is Back 4 Blood is a joke and a terrible marketing strategy. Folks, Left 4 Dead and Left 4 Dead 2 has SO much that you can appreciate about it. From the face animations, common infected death animations, flashlight shadow rendering, destructive environments, the musical score, survivor dialogue, diversified common infected (depending on the areas i.e airport, hospital, etcetera), a diverse cast of survivors that work together in unison, the survivor backstories (especially Zoey's brutal background story in the L4D comics), just the list goes on and ON.

If I hadn't convinced you to get this game and play it now, I don't know what to tell ya. It's a fun experience and especially fun with friends. There's tons of re-playability at only a price tag of 10 USD and you'll find yourself having "oh, I never knew that was a thing!" moments. To this day, this game still surprises me with cool new things I never realized. Do yourselves a favor, folks. Get L4D and L4D2, get some friends (if you can), and go play. 10/10 game.

[h1]Innovative and Timeless: A Co-Op Classic[/h1]

[i]From Valve (the creators of Counter-Strike, Half-Life and more) comes Left 4 Dead, a co-op action horror game that casts up to four players in an epic struggle for survival against swarming zombie hordes and terrifying mutant monsters.[/i]

[h2]Story[/h2]
The story is minimal and told through gameplay, environmental storytelling, and dialogue rather than cutscenes or traditional narrative exposition. The game takes place in the aftermath of a sudden outbreak of a mutagenic virus that turns people into zombie-like creatures known as the Infected. You play as one of four Survivors: Bill, Zoey, Francis or Louis. Left 4 Dead is divided into four campaigns/episodes, each like an episode in a zombie movie.

[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
Left 4 Dead 2 is a co-op survival horror FPS, playable with up to 4 players or bots. It combines fast-paced shooting with teamwork, strategy, and dynamic AI for unpredictable playthroughs. Enemy and item spawns vary each game, keeping the experience fresh. Teamwork is critical; if a player is incapacitated, others must help. Each campaign has multiple levels called chapters. Your goal is to get to the safe room alive at the end of the level. Each campaign has multiple chapters ending with a dramatic finale, defending a position until rescue.

[b][u]Weapons[/u][/b]
You always start with the M1911 semiautomatic pistol, the only weapon with unlimited ammo and usable while incapacitated. A second pistol allows dual-wielding, but there are no other secondary weapons. Melee is limited to shoving infected away.

The game features five primary weapons split into two tiers: Tier 1 includes the Pump Shotgun and SMG, while Tier 2 offers the Auto Shotgun, Assault Rifle, and Hunting Rifle. You also have two types of grenades: the Pipe Bomb, which lures enemies before exploding, and the Molotov Cocktail, which sets the ground and infected on fire.

[b][u]Game Modes[/u][/b]
There are two more game modes besides the Campaign:
[list][*][b]Versus[/b] — Two teams of up to 4 players alternate roles between Survivors and Infected. Survivors trying to reach the safe room. Special Infected trying to stop them. Scoring is based on how far survivors get and how much damage the Infected cause.
[*][b]Survival[/b] — Survive for as long as possible against endless waves of Infected in a small, enclosed area. Bronze, Silver, and Gold medals awarded based on time survived.[/list]
[h2]Enemies & Bosses[/h2]
There are 6 enemy types:
[list][*][b]Common Infected[/b] — The most commonly faced enemy and are the easiest to defeat. Their strength lies in their tendency to attack in large groups of up to several dozen, known as Hordes. They also run fast.
[*][b]Boomer[/b] — Can vomit on the player or explode in bile when killed. Getting any of it on you will attract hordes.
[*][b]Hunter[/b] — Lurking in the shadows and pounces from a distance. If it jumps on you, it will immobilize and claw down all your health until another player saves you.
[*][b]Smoker[/b] — Uses a long tongue to ensnare and drag the Survivors back to it. Same as with the Hunter, the Smoker will drain your health unless saved from another Survivor.
[*][b]Tank[/b] — Mini-boss. A massive, powerful brute that requires the whole team of Survivors to take down its large health pool.
[*][b]Witch[/b] — Mini-boss. Generally only appears a few times per campaign. Sitting down and crying loudly. She is passive and will not attack unless provoked by flashlights, gunfire, or Survivors in close proximity.[/list]
[h2]Environment[/h2]
Left 4 Dead features four original campaigns and two DLC campaigns, all with their own distinctive look and scenery. The general theme is a post-apocalyptic and desolate atmosphere with dark, moody and foggy areas, creating suspense. Certain areas require players to trigger noisy events, like lowering a bridge, which attracts hordes. These places often have weapons, stationary machine guns, ammo, med kits, etc. Gas cans, oxygen tanks and propane tanks can be found and strategically placed. Shooting them creates either a fire on the ground or an explosion.

[h2]Visual Design & Sound Design[/h2]
Color palettes and visual themes shift by campaign. Grays and blues in No Mercy, greens and browns in Blood Harvest, warm industrial tones in Dead Air. The blood splatter and gore is good and satisfying. Fog is used to limit vision and increase suspense. The UI is minimalistic and clean, and teammate outlines glow through walls in specific colors for coordination.

Sound design plays a crucial role in the game. It’s important to hear when Special Infected is nearby so you can prepare, and they all have their own distinct sounds. Calm piano music plays during safe moments; chaotic music intensifies during hordes. The voice acting is okay.

[h2]Constructive Criticism[/h2]
Very limited content at launch, but got a few updates later that added more content, but it still lacked content in my opinion.

Close-quarter combat is also very limited, as there are no melee weapons available.

No character/weapon customization, leveling, or unlockables. Each game is a clean slate, balancing play but limiting long-term motivation.

Playing either solo or co-op with bots can be annoying. The bot AI was not very good as they had poor pathfinding and often got stuck or failed to save you. They wouldn’t use throwables or perform coordinated attacks either.

Only a few Special Infected types. While well-designed, they become predictable over time.

Lack of map variety and environmental diversity. While the campaigns have unique themes, they often reused similar urban and rural assets.

[h2]The Verdict[/h2]
Despite the flaws, Left 4 Dead was an original game at launch. It was one of the first truly dedicated co-op first-person shooters. The game pioneered the concept of a game where players had to work together to survive, and this concept heavily influenced subsequent titles in the genre. A good game even to this day.

[h2]Rating: 8/10[/h2]

"What's the point of Left 4 Dead if Left 4 Dead [b] 2 [/b] exists?" is probably what you ask when you see this product.

It's difficult to 100% articulate and point into words what makes 1 still enjoyable even when 2 exists, but I think one of the main things that does is how barebones it is compared to 2. There is a lack of equipment to use, less special variety, less maps, no workshop support (although does support mods / addons). Just overall LESS of everything.

But for some reason, it feels grounded, it feels limiting, it feels... scarier? From the hud elements, musical cues, to the level design and atmosphere, Left 4 Dead simply just "feels" more scary and more gritty compared to 2. Expert in this game feels absolutely terrifying.

I like to play Left 4 Dead when I want a more barebones experience. You might think I'm crazy, maybe it's just workshop / addon fatigue, but I just find myself reaching for this more lately compared to 2.

Also when you die you ragdoll, huge plus.

The simple crux of playing Left 4 Dead is that Left 4 Dead 2 exists. The sequel has more of just about everything, with nearly all of this game's content included. This game has fewer campaigns, fewer extra modes, and fewer weapons (including a complete lack of melee weapons). I've seen some favor this game for its atmosphere. Indeed, Left 4 Dead takes itself more seriously, skewer closer to its horror inspiration. But I suppose that's not why I play either Left 4 Dead game, especially given that both are multiplayer-oriented experiences. When playing with friends, much of the tonal nuance is inevitably lost.
I will concede that, from my estimation, this game's default lighting solution is far more playable than the sequel's. You'll still find plenty of pitch-black rooms, but it's not as prohibitive.
If I can praise anything unequivocally, it's this game's opening cinematic, which expertly introduces you to so many key gameplay elements, such as the various special infected to expect and the car alarms.
As I see it, there's no reason to play this game when you can get basically all of its content in the sequel, on top of everything it adds. This game has few advantages over its successor to justify choosing it over the sequel.

As the core concept is the same for both games, I will cover both [i]Left 4 Dead[/i] (released November, 2008) and it's sequel, [i]Left 4 Dead 2[/i] as a single game. The core plot is the same for both games: You and three other players have to survive the zombie apocalypse and reach the end goal. Along the way, you pick up guns and ammo, explosives, and first aid. All four of you have to survive to the end, or be overwhelmed by the zombie horde. Got it? Go play.

In the past ten years, the gaming landscape is littered with multi-player games that have launched, had their moment in their sun, then the players go on to another game, and soon the game publishers shut down the servers. Yet, when you look at the gaming numbers for the [i]Left 4 Dead[/i] series, with 25K peak players for [i]Left 4 Dead 2[/i] in the week of this posting (and 1,062 for [i]Left 4 Dead[/i]) according to [url=http://markholtz.info/steamdb]SteamDB[/url]. It's easy to see why. The graphics, although slightly dated, still hold up in modern computers. The core gaming mechanics are easy to pick up within a few games. I particularly liked the horror motif, especially since it feels like you are part of a survival horror movie that runs around 60-90 minutes. I also like that you and three other players have to cooperate with each other, although there are some alternative gaming modes as well. The second game is open to mods.... wide open to mods. And, it is compatible across multiple platforms. 

Yet, when I am looking at this game, I cannot feel but annoyance at Valve as a game developer. The last game released by Valve was five years ago with [i]DOTA 2[/i]. The [i]Left 4 Dead[/i] games are overdue for a third release, but none is coming. We won't even speak of [i]Half Life 3[/i]. 

Would I recommend the games? Yes, but with qualifications.

The sequel, [i]Left 4 Dead 2[/i] is [b]HIGHLY RECOMMENDED[/b]. Not only is it an improved game from the original, but all of the missions from the first game have been transferred to the sequel as well. The online player base is larger as well, plus support for more playing modes and there is a GeForce Experience profile. The game got highly discounted during the last Steam Summer sale as well, thus it's worth waiting for a sale.

The original, [i]Left 4 Dead[/i], on the other hand, is [b]NOT RECOMMENDED[/b]. All of the missions from the original game has been ported to the sequel, and the sequel is better supported and has a bigger online population. Save the money.

I was confused when I first put the disc in all those years ago and was told I had to download something called Steam from some company called Valve. I was familiar with Half Life and Portal, but not with the company that made them. So the one good thing I can say about this game is that it introduced me to Steam, which I suspect was the whole point. I feel like this game was always just a virus to infect as many computers with Steam as possible. This is a very flawed game that for some reason is considered immune to criticism by its many fans. Simplistic. Minimalist. Repetitive. No character progression or customization. You do not unlock new characters, weapons, attachments, abilities, or anything. Every level is exactly the same with a linear path to follow and no real incentive to explore. A few hours of mindless fun, followed by a pointless grind. The excuse has always been, "It's meant to be multiplayer. You're supposed to play it with friends." Do you like doing the same thing over and over again? Because I sure don't. Neither do my friends. This game is one of many that represents a dark turning point in the history of the video game industry when things like offline and single player started to go out of style, when you needed to create an account and install a special program just to play, when developers once again began to use repetition in place of actual content. If you had told me ten years ago that this type of game would become the norm, I would have laughed in your face. I thought it was just a minor cold. Surely we could just take some medicine, get some sleep, and it would all disappear like a bad dream. But now, there is a plague of these kinds of games that provide about 10 minutes of content and put it on a dizzying, endless loop. I think I'm going to be sick. Excuse me while I throw up, question my life choices, have an existential crisis, and find a good single player game to wash this horrible taste out of my mouth.

While I wouldn't call myself a Left 4 Dead fan, I am very passionate about this game and the sequel, even to the point where I've played all of Back 4 Blood for some reason. In general, Left 4 Dead 2 is one of my favourite video games of all time, would be my favourite zombie (or infected, whatever) game if it weren't for plants vs zombies garden warfare, yes I am being serious. I love almost everything about this duology, from the gunplay to the artwork to the story to the mods to even the menu design, it is all impressive. Not my favourite duology because of reasons mentioned two sentences ago, but still very much up there. Here's the thing however, one thing I have intentionally excluded from the list is the characters, which are famously what makes L4D so good in so many of the playerbase's eyes. And I agree, most of the characters are reasonable, emotionally deep and realistic characters meaning you can sympathise with them, understand their struggles and make yourself feel like you truly are fighting alongside them in a chaotic post-apocalyptic world. But notice how I said "most". Now I don't have a unique or witty way of saying this so I'm just going to do what every other over-dramatic person in this situation would do, that being to say it as it is but with caps lock on so that I can emphasise my point: ZOEY IS ONE OF THE WORST VIDEO GAME CHARACTERS EVER CONCEIVED BY MANKIND AND I WISH SHE WAS THE ONE THAT DIED INSTEAD OF- whoops almost just spoiled the end of a 15 year old  game everyone has definitely already played by now there, remind me not to do that again when I do another negative review. Anyway here's why.

I don't know if saying that Zoey is a badly written character is an unpopular opinion or whatever, but I do wanna say no offence to the writers or voice actor playing Zoey in the slightest, the writers did an incredible job in other places and the voice actor did a great job in general. Zoey just feels like a side character in an 80's text-based adventure game, so whether the writers were being overworked with 2 hours of sleep when making her or she was made by a 12 year old on a "bring your son/daughter to work day", I wouldn't be surprised either way. But what makes Zoey such a bad character? Well I promise I will actually answer that question this time in the next paragraph.

I want you to consider the other characters in Left 4 Dead 1 to start. You've got Louis, a successful business man with no combat experience in the slightest, and who probably has a pill fetish if the L4D community is a reliable source. There's Francis, a biker dude not used to working in a team with strangers, but is still willing to lend a hand to the group of survivors he has found himself in. And then there's Bill, a war veteran who clearly has a lot of experience with combat and gunplay, but zombies is a whole other story for him. Now try and describe Zoey's character. This is problem #1, Zoey is a boring character with nothing unique or distinct about her. She's just some random person who ended up in the zombie apocalypse alongside three other far more interesting characters. Now I get it, complaining that she has little backstory and saying that that alone is the reason why she is a bad character is a harsh thing to say, which is why I would also like to bring up the fact that she has basically no character development at all, both in changes to her as a person as well as traits she adopts throughout. Now admittedly, this is a part of Left 4 Dead 1's story that was lacking a bit, there is barely any character development in general, but in this case, you'd think they'd go all in on Zoey having the character development, but in the end even Francis ends up having more than her. Zoey is more one-dimensional than a Back 4 Blood character. In fact, look at Left 4 Dead 2: pretty much every character is unique and changes their attitudes to the zombies, each other and the impact of the apocalypse on their futures, something Zoey seems to be physically incapable of doing. Now I'm going to change the subject out of fear of repeating myself again.

Whether Zoey also looking like a really boring character as well as playing like one was intentional or not I don't know because I'm not a secret agent at valve trying to see whether people would care about Zoey dying in Left 4 Dead 3 coming out in around 20 years time. I know it sounds bizarre, but hear me out. Just by looking at the characters you can see how equipped or unequipped each character is for the zombie apocalypse, from the one in a business suit to another in full army uniform. Zoey is wearing a bland red jacket and jeans. Again, I get it, maybe her looking like a regular person was intentional to show just how unpredictable the outbreak was and how any one of us could be in such a situation any day now. Still though, what are we supposed to make of that? That she likes wearing that particular kind of outfit? The plain features don't say much in terms of her non-existent personality or her interests of literally nothing, unless it's meant to represent youth? In which case, ok, but why make that her entire character? Anyway, you're probably wondering why I mentioned earlier about her playing like a  boring character given how the character difference is completely cosmetic and each character plays the same. Well no offence to the voice actor once again, but the actual lines given for Zoey really don't help with character building or establishing her as a human being capable of doing human being things. Also I don't know if anybody else experiences this, but why does the Zoey AI absolutely hate me? No joke, when I play singleplayer, Zoey always shoots the witch whenever possible, shoots gas canisters when teammates are nearby, uses the only medkit on herself when she has the most health of the entire team (usually in the green too) and completely refuses to revive teammates, even when all the infected are dead. As if hating Zoey couldn't get any easier.

I think one of the reasons I hate Zoey so much is just seeing how well the characters in Left 4 Dead 2 were done. L4D2 probably has my favourite cast of multiple main characters of any video game due to just how contrasting they are in addition to how well they go together. watching as Roachelle basically becomes like a mother to the entire group despite clearly having no experience with that kind of thing before, or seeing how Nick goes from being a snide asshole to everyone to really letting his light shine through in their darkest moments is really heartwarming, even in a grim zombie-ridden world. Coach and Ellis' humour despite their worst fears coming to fruition is also charming, making these characters not only easy for each other to love, but for the player to love too. It's a shame that Zoey never got this treatment, sure there was not much potential when you really summarise her character, but considering how much less inspiration there might have been for other valve characters, I know they could have done so much better.

I understand some people might defend Zoey or whatever, well good for you, more power to you in fact. I just wanted to complain about how terrible of a video game character Zoey is in my opinion, and not even for valve's standards, I'm comparing her to characters from games like Far Cry 6 and Saints Row 2022. If you think Zoey is a good character, that's fine, just know I am going to disagree with you unless you actually give a reason or reasons as to why, because I am seriously struggling to think of a single one. I know valve won't see this because they despise listening to their community, especially on the topic of their games, but at least they lay the foundations for wonderful communities to sprout in their wake. If only I could bring myself to give this beautiful game a positive review, unfortunately Zoey exists. So yeah, TL;DR: Zoey sucks.

A few years ago this game may have been fun, however now that Left 4 Dead 2 is out for the same price this game feels obsolete and overpriced. I will compare the differences between the games that I've noticed and you can come to your own decision of wheather it is worth the price.

Left 4 Dead 2 includes:
Almost all of the original's content. (For example: Weapons, infected and levels.)
New skins. (For example: The pistols look more realistic and the smoker is easier to see in the distance.)
New levels. (For example: The daytime levels, this feature wasn't included in the first game.)
New infected. (For example: Jockey, Charger and Spitter.)
New weapons. (For example: The Spas Shotgun and Grenade Launcher.)
Smoother gameplay features. (For example: Friendly fire is disabled while you are down.)
More gamemodes. (For examples: The mutation modes like Flu Season and TANK!!!!!!!!!!)
Less glitches. (For example: In the first game's level 'No Mercy' you can fall through the lift and die.)
Addons. (You can download community content and customize your game.)
Larger community. (For all these reasons.)

Left 4 Dead 1 includes:
Much nicer animations. (For example: When you pull the health kit out it flops in your hands.)
New sounds. (In the recycled levels for Left 4 Dead 2 the zombies use the Left 4 Dead 2 noises.)

That's about everything. In conclusion, Left 4 Dead 2 has much more content but ultimately it's your decision. Have fun killing zombies. ;)

This isn't inherently a bad game, but in 2019, it's hard to have a positive experience.

Before I even discuss the game, I need to mention the community's abnormal toxicity levels. Many veterans are vehemently toxic against new players or just everyone in general. Team killing is enabled, which means you will regularly get downed by people for your lack of skill as you try and learn the ropes, while they clip their mic audio shouting racist slurs at you. There are nice people that play this game too, but the few bad apples seem disproportionately numerous and vocal.

Beyond that, the servers are just about dead. Versus mode only has occasional matches going, I have yet to find a full Survival mode lobby, and there are only 2 or 3 campaign choices going at any one time. There are a bunch of custom player servers you can join, but these modify the game in weird ways they won't explain, and their players usually rip apart noobs anyway. If you start your own lobby, a couple of people may trickle in here and there, but it's uncommon. Your best bet is to have a group of people ready to play with you, otherwise you will likely struggle to gain any traction in the multiplayer.

Fortunately, most of the content can be experienced as a single player with bots. This is not the ideal way to play. The bots just aren't skilled enough to handle the higher difficulties, and they aren't able to navigate around the game's randomized challenges in a satisfying way. For example, in the last hour of play before writing this review, I had two instances where the AI screwed up my run. In one instance, a witch spawned immediately next to the level exit, and none of the bots were willing to approach the door to move on. This voided an achievement I was going for. In another instance, I was in the escape vehicle at the very end of a 30-minute campaign, and the bots got confused and never entered with me. Eventually a creature called a Tank entered the vehicle and pummelled me to death, again rendering an achievement unobtainable.

I am mentioning achievements because there is a significant lack of other ways to measure your advancement in the game. There's no sense of progress - no unlockables, no leveling, no story, no real reason to even survive a campaign because the credits roll and....nothing happens. A game doesn't need progress to be fun, but I found myself looking for reasons to play each campaign more than once or twice.

Left 4 Dead heavily relies on random item and enemy placement for replayability, because there is VERY little content here to play. There are a total of 6 campaigns, and they can each be completed in 20 minutes or so on easy. The hardest difficulty can make campaigns take over an hour. And that's all you get! A few different modes using the same maps don't help to make this game feel any fuller.

The gameplay itself is decent for a game of this age. It can be satisfying to feel hordes of zombies melt under your gunfire, and there is a definite visceral rush to getting overwhelmed by mobs or attacked by a variety of "special infected". Limping to the next safehouse on painkillers can feel like survival horror, while cornering up with a skilled team and controlling a very dangerous situation is cathartic.

Unfortunately, the presentation is headache-inducing. The Source engine was never good for dark environments, since light sources don't spread out properly. This means that you're often swinging your head wildly to see the entirety of a pitch-black room with a small shaft of flashlight in the center of your screen. It's very fatiguing on the eyes. Zombies meanwhile are all practically colorless, and you have to strain to make out shapes in the gloom. The audio design is even worse - the weapons are FAR too loud and repetitive. When a 30 minute campaign has literal thousands of zombies to kill, there is rarely a quiet moment through the constant gunfire. Zombies are, as you would expect, shrieking and awful. Were it not for sound being an important part of strategy, I would have gladly played this game on mute.

This game may have been fun in its heyday, but over a decade later, I really couldn't recommend it to anyone but the rare gamer that will have a group ready to check out an old game together. The community is toxic, the bots are stupid, the content is slim, and the overall presentation is terribly ugly.

[h1] Retro Review[/h1] 
Now I bought this game a while ago mostly out of curiosity. Are people playing this game still? And is it the same as I remember?

[u] Gameplay[/u] 
I probably don’t have to explain the gameplay basics as its one of these games everyone already has played a lot or will never play as left for dead 2 exists. Most people playing this game do it solely for the nostalgia or achievements.

Now there is something I want to mention that I always disliked in this game. The enemy variety, gameplay itself was always fantastic but I always didn’t like in the first game the weapon balancing. There are only 5 weapons excluding the pistol. After a while in a map, you are usually given the choice of 3 weapon upgrades, either an assault rifle, automatic shotgun, or hunting rifles. I barely know anyone using the hunting rifle, and most of the time the automatic shotgun is better in almost every situation.

Anyways, I was really surprised that no matter which daytime I played I always found a single game or so going, albeit often people from far away countries, Brazil and such which makes the game kind of dead. For me the game had a weird bug on windows 10, making it a mess to play. Every once in a while, the game will freeze and I can continue playing like a couple minutes later usually being my death in a fight. Also, there are some griefers out there, outright abusing the console to join anytime and kicking people without votes. Weird that this isn’t fixed until this day making some weird spergs that solely want to go to other peoples games and kick everyone.

[u]Aesthetics [/u] 
Graphically I always had it way much better in mind. Some stuff like the fingers of the main characters or indoor models look really dated. On the other hand, player models itself, zombies (especially their ragdoll physics) and lighting effects are still really great. Animations itself are really neat and the more horror focused soundtrack is something that people liked more about the first game than the second.

[u]Conclusion/TL;DR [/u] 
Generally, you can still find people to play this game with without a problem. The thing is the game didn’t want to run that well for me, and I managed to encounter a griefer or two. I've had a pretty good time playing this game. It's aged remarkably well for a game with 30 years just around the corner. The Director is still one of the most advanced systems I've ever seen in a video game. However, it has an unintended consequence: it forces you to play very fast, and this can break immersion. If you are afraid of the zombies in even the slightest you will fail repeatedly and your resources will dwindle. So, the best solution is to not be afraid - and you are greatly rewarded for this. Once you learn the zombies really aren't as threatening as they sound, the game just gets very easy. Speaking of sound, this game is full of amazing sounds. Terrifying, unsettling sounds. There were so many moments were I was huddled in a corner looking for the source of some foreign rumbling just to realize it was another Common Infected sound I hadn't heard yet. The music is incredible and so crucial to the gameplay, a big part of why it has left such an impression on so many players (the other part being that it is just well written music). Another great thing about this game is that it's actually very well balanced. For the most part, nothing ever feels unfair or insurmountable. Unless your teammates make it so, which brings me to my next point: the bots.

The bots are just stupid. Unbearably stupid. They don't understand how to avoid witches to the point that if you are forced to pass one, she is guaranteed to be startled after you pass her. Their target priority is generally awful. They have a logical hierarchy (Bosses, Special Infected, Common Infected), but don't react to live or fluid situations well. They struggle greatly to navigate the environment well, are often in the worst possible place at all times and Smokers. Oh, my god Smokers. For some reason, these boneheads can only conceive of shoving the grabbed player to break the Smoker's tongue. They won't shoot it, won't shoot it's tongue, and certainly won't react to anything attacking you while you are grabbed. They just mindlessly walk at you until they can get into melee range the majority of the time. It's insufferable. They refuse to heal when they need to, refuse to accept no for answer when healing isn't needed, and just don't pick up items under any circumstances and wouldn't use them if they fell from the sky into their pockets anyway. That said, they actually do have incredible aim and will take out anything it seems aside from a Tank or Witch in seconds, sometimes before you can even react. 

Audio design is great, the game is stylish and intuitive, the levels are unique and interesting, the enemies are awesome and fun. This game packs a lot into such a small box. The only reason I don't recommend it is because there isn't much to experience beyond the singleplayer campaigns. I couldn't figure out how to mod this game, so that part may be on me, but the servers are dead. The few people still playing it are not very fun to play with, either speedrunning levels in seconds with the expectation that you will keep up, or just doing... nothing. Like nothing. At all. Wandering aimlessly. But you won't have to worry about that, because odds are when you are logged on, you won't find any lobbies anyway.

There's no reason to spend the money on this game. There wouldn't even be a justification for the storage space if it were free.

I mean none of this as criticism of the game. Obviously, Left 4 Dead was not made with a sequel in mind, and what the devs have done in Left 4 Dead 2 is worthy of praise, not critique, but that does mean that is the reality for this game.

I found Left4Dead to be very very over rated. 
Ok, I liked the suspense, the thrill when you begin to play this apocalyptic game, which derives from the dark gloomy survival atmosphere and the zombie hordes that rush at you. But that feeling of tension lasts only 3,4 hours.  
Then you understand the biggest downside of this game: 
1) it's incredibly repetitive. All the missions are the same. Kill the zombies - the regular ones and the 4 special types (smoker, hunter, boomer and tank) and endure the hordes that spawn every minute. And of course get to the safe zone. 
2) The maps feel empty, and not very interactive (not much to destroy or blow up). 
3) There isn't anything to buy, upgrade or build (for example, why not having the possibility to build some defense system like walls, spikes, traps etc...?).
4) The environment is way too dark. I understand that it's a post-apocalyptic game and that the power went out everywhere. But still.....it is annoying to have to plow through all those dark maps, because it subtracts from the enjoyment of exploration. 
5) The multiplayer experience is poor. It is good that I first finished the campains on singleplayer and only then I played them in multiplayer - because the great majority of players moved on to Left4Dead 2 and Left4Blood. The ones that still play rush mindlessly to the end of the mission, so you can't take your time to explore and you can't play properly/realistically - which is to stick together and play carefully. Also there are a lot of hackers and trols. Multiplayer is ok only if you play with your steam friends, and especially if you play with your real life friends. 
6) There are some extra modalities but they are badly done - "versus" where one team play as monsters and one team as survivors - it is unbalanced and chaotic. "Survival" is just the "hold the fort" version of the maps - which is very hard - and only possible to finish with gold medal when you play alongside experienced and serious players. 
7) I didn't like that you can carry only 1 weapon, 1 health pack and 1 bomb- which can be a problem on singleplayer because the bots cannot carry bombs. 
8) The hordes rush at you every minute - after a while it gets annoying. 
It's not a bad game, I had a lot of hours of fun. But the thing is - only the first few hours are really great-thrilling entertainment and the rest is just repetitive grinding to the end. As a foreword, I'd like to point out that despite not recommending this game, that should not imply that it's bad. Before I go any further, I'll say that the biggest reason I'm not recommending this game is because its sequel - Left 4 Dead 2 - is practically a more refined version of the same product, plus more. The second big reason is because this game's community is utterly revolting. I've met my fair share of trolls, griefers, bullies and a couple other words I can't write in this review, and it genuinely defeats one of Left 4 Dead's biggest qualities: the encouragement of cooperative play. When a game designed for four-player action becomes more appealing (and relaxing) when playing offline with the bots, there is a big problem there. I could write a whole review on why I hate L4D's community so much, but I'd rather not go there. 
Let's discuss some good things about Left 4 Dead. 
Set in October 2009, the world has been engulfed by a virus known as the Green Flu, which has turned pretty much everyone into a zombie. And I don't mean the George Romero type zombie that shambles to you at a snail's pace, I mean the rabid, snarling things from 28 Days Later. As you would expect from a game with SPRINTING zombies, Left 4 Dead is a pulse-pounding ride that holds, in my opinion, some of the most addicting game-play I've ever witnessed. It's just pure fun, and extremely gory fun at that. You make your way through abandoned environments throughout Pennsylvania that have become overrun with the infected, from ghostly metropolises, small towns, all the way to the woods of the Allegheny (a real place). Much like Valve's masterpiece game series Half-Life, Left 4 Dead employs a minimalist attitude when it comes to cutscenes and talky-talky bits, making the pace of the game very easy-going, but at the sacrifice of world-building and story-telling. The four-minute introduction that plays at the start of the game is without a doubt one of my all-time favourite game cutscenes, and what's more, it mirrors the intensity of how the game actually plays out once you take control. If that isn't a good sign I don't know what is. 
All D.L.C is completely free, which is great, though I wouldn't say you'd be missing much if you skipped them. The four protagonists are incredibly well-crafted, and have great chemistry and personality. At times they can all be downright funny too, and I still laugh out loud whenever I hear their manic laughter and death-screams. 
The weapon variety is a little bland, but this isn't really a game where it would matter all that much anyway. The special infected (smokers, boomers, hunters, tanks and witches) all unite to create a fearsome opposition for your team, and are so much fun to play as in versus mode. Beware, playing in versus is easily the most toxic aspect of this game. You will most likely be kicked for simply being a better player than the enemy team. There is also a survival mode, but it's really only about as fun and inspired as it sounds. 
As with most Valve games, a very intriguing developer commentary is included, and this is always a very awesome thing that more developers need to take note of. 
So far I have described what most would call a good game, but the big issue here is that Left 4 Dead 2 literally includes all the campaigns in this game (D.L.C included), with even more stuff added on top. For this exact reason, and in the interest of your own money, I cannot recommend Left 4 Dead. If you are curious about this series, and aren't a completionist like me, just go play Left 4 Dead 2. That game isn't perfect, but it's the complete package regardless. All in all, this game is still plenty of fun standing on its own two feet, and if you're fortunate enough to have three friends to join you, (or seven for versus) you're bound to kill some serious hours slaying the undead getting to safety. Definitely play a campaign on expert difficulty for that true survivalist experience. As an experienced player, I prefer advanced over normal difficulty - it's that sweet spot for a challenge. But like I said, go with Left 4 Dead 2. This game is better off left for... ah, never mind.
